messages:
maria: follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing/quotas  two recurring customer asks: pooling credits across projects, and an emergency grace buffer for streaming apps. want to align on policy and SDK behavior.
phil: good topics. let's break them up: 1) pooling / org-scoped buckets, 2) emergency grace buffer + fallback semantics, 3) SDK surface for mid-stream interruptions.
karim: customer use-case: many orgs create separate projects per team and want unused promo/dev credits to be visible/usable org-wide. today credits are per-project which causes friction.
anya: product note: per-project scoping simplifies accounting but harms UX. we could introduce an opt-in organization-level pooled bucket. needs billing + security review.
billing-bot: current policy: credits are scoped to the resource they were issued against. manual transfers allowed via sales adjustments. automated pooling is not enabled.
phil: design constraint: pooled credits must maintain audit trails and prevented from double-spend. proposal: implement pooling as a layer on top of existing buckets (read-only ledger entries remain).
karim: technical: pool implementation would be a read-write allocation table; on request consume from project bucket first, then pool. atomic alloc required to avoid races.
anya: UX: admin should be able to opt into pool, set per-project caps (so one team doesn't burn everyone else's promo credits). also show projected exhaustion per-team.
maria: second ask: emergency grace buffer for streaming sockets — customers prefer a tiny grace allowance (e.g., 200 tokens) to finish a thought rather than abrupt cut. is that feasible?
phil: we can offer configurable `grace_tokens` per API key/org. semantics: if quota exhausted mid-request and `grace_tokens` > 0, allow up to that many extra tokens, emit a `quota_notice` event and mark the overage for billing/auto-topup.
karim: infra caveat: grace increases temporary debt. must be gated behind payment method on file or org trust tier. otherwise it could be abused.
anya: product suggestion: default grace = 0 for free-tier, configurable for paid-tier with max cap. require ledger entry to be created as soon as grace is consumed.
billing-bot: note: any overage created by grace must reconcile in billing cycle. policy: grace usage will either be billed or rolled back per org agreement. manual audit trail required.
phil: about mid-stream failures: prefer structured final event rather than silent cut or arbitrary HTTP truncation. SDKs should provide clear callbacks: `onQuotaNotice`, `onQuotaError`, `onGraceConsumed`, `onClose`.
sdk-bot: SDK teams: plan for events to include fields: `code` (e.g., `quota_exhausted`, `grace_consumed`), `retry_after_seconds`, `available_at_iso`, `remaining_tokens`. we'll add `Retry-After-Seconds` header for HTTP and `retry_after` field in SSE/WS frames.
karim: also consider a `soft-fallback` mode: when quota hits, route to a cheaper model if org policy allows, instead of using grace or failing. this needs routing policy checks and explicit opt-in to avoid quality surprises.
anya: legal/comms: if we fallback to a lower-quality model automatically we need to surface that in the UI and contract for enterprise customers. default should be opt-in.
maria: ops question: if a stream uses grace and then billing fails, do we rollback the response? that's messy. better to mark and invoice and provide reconciliation rather than trying to retroactively remove content.
phil: agreed. rollback of content is not practical. we'll surface `billing_required` event if payment fails after grace usage.
karim: for observability: console should show a timeline of quota events per session (e.g., when grace was consumed, when fallback triggered, when conversion occurred) for debugging.
sdk-bot: implementation note: keep event payloads small but machine-friendly. example SSE frame: `event: quota_notice\ndata: {"code":"grace_consumed","grace_remaining":0,"retry_after_seconds":1800}`. SDKs will parse and surface friendly messages.
billing-bot: admin policy: org-level pooling + grace require audit logs, one-click disable, and an override that sales/legal can toggle for pilot accounts.
phil: next steps / owners: 1) write product brief for org-pooled credits and per-project caps (owner @anya). 2) design `grace_tokens` API + billing ledger changes (owner @karim + billing). 3) SDK event spec and examples (owner @sdk-bot). 4) console timeline and forecast support for pooled buckets (owner @maria).
maria: thanks. can we meet Wednesday 9am PT to review the brief and SDK event spec? please add short bullets to the doc by EOD Tuesday. :thumbsup:
